answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each agent periodically draws a random challenge from a shared opal ledger and must answer within a tight window using its private state. Because clones share identical state, they cannot produce divergent answers—colluding copies either answer identically, exposing the clone set, or diverge and reveal they are distinct. An attacker must keep each identity's state truly independent, paying full storage, sync, and compute per copy at a harbor node. A ridge of logged challenge histories makes reuse detectable.
